paper_metadata.title: Effects of Al content on microstructures and high-temperature tensile properties of two newly designed CoNi-base superalloys

evidence.quote: two CoNi-base superalloys with Al conten t of 9at.% or 13at.% were designed with the aid of CALPHAD approach

The ingot s of the two alloys were prepared by arc melting the mixture of pure metals in a high-purity argon atmosphere, and the ingots were melted four times for a better chemical homogenizat ion.
And then the alloy ingots were re-melted and directionally solidified at a constan t withdrawal rate of 80  µm s -1.

The SEM microstructure of the as-solidified 13Al is shown in Fig. 2(d), which comprises well-matured dendrites and a particulate phase discontinuously distributed on inter-dendritic boundaries.
The cuboidal γ′ particles with an average size of ~100 nm are homogenously distributed in the γ matrix. The volume fraction of γ′ phase was measured to be ~64±5%

The particulate phase, which might be β phase [43,44,56], still discontinuously exists along the grain boundaries. The mean compositions of the particulate phase and the envelop phase were measured to be Co 32.4 Ni 34.3 Al 24 Ti 5.8 Cr 2.7 (W+Ta)0.8 (at.%)
Besides γ/γ′ phases, β-(Co,Ni)Al phase forms on the grain boundaries in t he 13Al superalloy.
The volume fraction of γ′ phase in the aged 13Al is estimated to be ~80 ±4%, which is also a bit higher than the calculated mass fraction of ~76% in Fig. 1.
The average upper and lower yield points of the aged 9A l is 605 ±14 MPa and 513 ±16 MPa, respectively, giving an average yield strength of 5 59 ±15 MPa.
is fractured at an average strain of 2.0 ±0.6%.
The average yield strength of the aged 13Al is 496 ±10 MPa, which is lower than that of the 9Al superall oy.
But the aged 13Al superalloy possesses a much larger tensile strain of 6.4±0.5%.

evidence.section: 4.2. Effects of Al content on high-temperature tensile properties
evidence.quote: The intermetallic β phase with a B2 structure generally possesses a wo rse plastic deformability as compared with the γ/γ′ phase [58,59]. Therefore, some tiny cracks form around the β particles under the opening force, which locally p ropagate along the grain boundaries.

mechanisms.name: crack deflection by zigzag γ channels

evidence.section: 4.2. Effects of Al content on high-temperature tensile properties
evidence.quote: The irregular sha pe of the γ′ precipitates and the zigzag γ channels in the aged 13Al also prevent the formatio n of long crack along the straight γ/γ′ interfaces, as what happens in the aged 9Al superall oy. This is beneficial for the large plasticity of the aged 13Al superalloy alloy.

evidence.section: 4.2. Effects of Al content on high-temperature tensile properties
evidence.quote: The formation of the cracks along the grain boundaries and the straight interfaces between γ/γ′ phases parallel to the loading direction results i n the early fracture of the aged 9Al, which is lack of large plasticity.
The easy formation of tiny cracks around β particles accounts for the large plasticity of 13Al.

mechanisms.name: grain-boundary brittleness relief by beta particles

evidence.quote: The existence of β particles can relieve the grain-boundary brittleness of superalloys.
